subject: Enclave segmentation briefing and walk-through materials for ACME private deployment

Subject: Enclave segmentation briefing and walk-through materials for ACME private deployment

Hi Jordan / ACME Security team,

Thanks for the call earlier — attaching the high-level enclave segmentation brief we promised and a PNG of the updated architecture overlay. The attached PDF includes:
- Enclave definitions (control, inference, telemetry)
- Inter-enclave traffic policies and allowed ports
- Keying material boundaries and KMS integration notes

Quick notes: the private deployment for ACME will use a dedicated VPC with three isolated enclaves. Traffic between the inference enclave and telemetry is routed through a hardened service proxy with mTLS and strict egress policies. We included configuration snippets for the service proxy in the text attachment.

Please review and flag any areas you'd like us to expand on before the walkthrough. We can do a live network walk-through Wednesday or Thursday next week.

Attachments: redwood-enclave-seg-v1.3.pdf (PDF), architecture-diagram-v2.png (PNG), enclave-config-snippets.txt (text)

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

From: Whitebox Audit <auditor@whiteboxsecurity.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-eng@acme.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Enclave segmentation briefing and walk-through materials for ACME private deployment

Marcus — thanks for sending this over. A quick read-through and a couple of clarifying requests before we go deeper:

1) In the diagram the control plane appears to have a management network pathway to the inference enclave. Can you confirm whether management-plane traffic traverses the same subnet or an out-of-band management interface?

2) For the KMS integration: are customer keys scoped per-tenant (ACME) and stored in their KMS, or does Redwood hold a wrapped key? We need exact wording for the SOC 2 narrative.

3) Can you provide the NAT/firewall rules that show egress deny-by-default exceptions (we only need the rule names and high-level intent, not raw configs)?

We expect to use these for the evidence bundle; if you can add one-page summaries for each of these items that would be ideal. Also confirm availability for a 60-minute walkthrough next Tue/Wed.

— Claire Mahoney
Lead Auditor, Whitebox Security
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Whitebox Audit <auditor@whiteboxsecurity.com>, security-eng@acme.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Enclave segmentation briefing and walk-through materials for ACME private deployment

Claire — good questions, quick answers below and I attached two one-page summaries as requested.

1) Management-plane separation: the management/control plane uses a dedicated management VPC peered to the tenant VPC with strict policy-based routing. Management traffic never traverses the inference tenant subnets; we terminate management interfaces on a dedicated interface that is reachable only from ops bastions. Summary: out-of-band management plane. (see "management-plane-summary" attachment)

2) KMS key handling: ACME will provision a customer-managed KMS key (BYOK) in their cloud account. Redwood performs envelope-wrapping but does NOT persist the unwrapped tenant key. The key material is only accessible to the Redwood control plane for key exchange operations and is audited. (see "kms-handling-summary")

3) Egress and firewall rule set: we operate deny-by-default egress at the enclave edge. Exceptions are tracked in a named rule set (ACME-PROD-EGRESS-EXCEPTIONS) and reviewed quarterly. I've included the rule set summary and a short table of the common exceptions (DNS, monitoring to telemetry endpoints over TLS, and OCSP).

Attached: management-plane-summary.pdf, kms-handling-summary.pdf

If it's helpful, we can export sanitized iptables/aws-nacl rule names for the bundle. For the walkthrough: Wed Nov 18 10:00am PT works for our infra leads (Sooj & Rishi). Marcus — can you confirm with ACME?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Principal Infra Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
